If you're feeling overwhelmed or considering self-harm, please know that there are people who want to support you. You don’t have to carry this alone.
If you are in immediate danger, please reach out to emergency services or go to the nearest emergency room. For confidential, free support available 24/7, you can connect with these resources:Crisis Text Line: Text HOME to 741741988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Dial or text 988 (in the US and Canada) or call 111 (in the UK).The Trevor Project (for LGBTQ youth): Call 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678-678.International Resources: You can find a directory of international suicide hotlines at findahelpline.com.Sometimes, when the urge to self-harm is strong, using a "harm reduction" technique can help the feeling pass without causing injury. Some people find relief by:Holding an ice cube in their hand until it melts.Snapping a rubber band against their wrist.Drawing on their skin with a red marker.Vigorously exercising or punching a pillow to release pent-up energy.Things can get better, and reaching out to a friend, family member, or a professional is a brave and important first step.
